question: For a PMMA rod in slow airflow at reduced oxygen in microgravity, which investigation varied flow speed, oxygen concentration and sample geometry such as rods?

answer.sentence: The investigation was BASS-II, whose objectives included studying flame behavior in microgravity and examining practical fuels in several geometries including rods.

citations.title: BASS-II: Objectives (PSI-25)
citations.quote: Study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity.

citations.title: BASS-II: Objectives (PSI-25)
citations.quote: Sample geometry (rods, spherical section, slabs, films, and fabric sheets

answer.sentence: Its approach varied the main variables of airflow speed and oxygen concentration, with oxygen reduced below 21% by adding nitrogen.

citations.title: BASS-II: Approach (PSI-25)
citations.quote: Main variables are airflow speed and oxygen concentration (oxygen varied below 21% by adding nitrogen).

answer.sentence: The tests were performed aboard the International Space Station in a small wind tunnel that could impose airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s.

citations.title: BASS-II: Approach (PSI-25)

question: What misconceptions about fires on spacecraft does the combustion researcher's guide list?

answer.sentence: The guide says earlier spacecraft fire-safety thinking included the mistaken belief that a steady fire cannot exist in a quiescent microgravity environment.

citations.title: A Researcher’s Guide to: Combustion Science, p. 35
citations.quote: A steady fire cannot exist in a quiescent microgravity environment.

answer.sentence: It also lists the misconception that a fire will self-extinguish if ventilation is shut off.

citations.title: A Researcher’s Guide to: Combustion Science, p. 35
citations.quote: A fire will self-extinguish if ventilation is shut off.

answer.sentence: A third misconception was that the reduced-gravity environment is inherently safer and that terrestrial fire standards and tests are therefore very conservative.

citations.title: A Researcher’s Guide to: Combustion Science, p. 35
citations.quote: the reduced-gravity environment is inherently safer, terrestrial fire standards and tests represent a very conservative approach to fire safety.

question: What kind of portable fire extinguisher was sent to the ISS to replace the CO2 units?

answer.sentence: The documents say that non-toxic water-mist portable fire extinguishers were designed for spaceflight, and the first two were sent to the ISS in December 2015 to replace CO2 units that were already onboard.

citations.title: A Researcher’s Guide to: Combustion Science, p. 26
citations.quote: non-toxic water-mist portable fire extinguishers were designed, tested, fabricated and certified for spaceflight

citations.title: A Researcher’s Guide to: Combustion Science, p. 26
citations.quote: The first two of the planned nine water-mist portable fire extinguishers were sent to the ISS in December 2015 to replace CO2 units that are currently onboard.

question: Which gaseous fire suppressants does FLEX measure the effectiveness of?

answer.sentence: FLEX measures the effectiveness of inert-gas suppressants including CO2, He, and SF6.

citations.title: FLEX: Objectives (PSI-69)
citations.quote: measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6

citations.title: FLEX: Research Impacts / Earth Benefits (PSI-69)
citations.quote: the effectiveness of various fire suppressants, including CO2, He, and SF6, in microgravity

answer.sentence: The guide also says FLEX studies heptane and methanol droplets in oxygen and nitrogen diluted with a second inert gas, specifically nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium or xenon.

citations.title: A Researcher’s Guide to: Combustion Science, p. 12
citations.quote: study heptane and methanol droplets in ambient mixtures of oxygen and nitrogen diluted with a second inert gas (nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium or xenon)

question: How did the airflow velocity in Saffire-III differ from Saffire-I?

answer.sentence: Saffire-III was conducted at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s, while Saffire-I was conducted at 20 cm/s, so Saffire-III used a higher airflow velocity.

citations.title: SAFFIRE-III: Approach (PSI-100)
citations.quote: the experiments were conducted at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s compared to 20 cm/s during Saffire I

citations.title: SAFFIRE-I: Approach (PSI-98)
citations.quote: Saffire-I was conducted at an air flow velocity of 20 cm/s.
